statement.p: A particle moves on a circle of radius 9 cm, centered at the origin, in the xy-plane (x and y measured in centimeters). At time t=0 it starts at the point (0,9) and moves counterclockwise as t increases, going once around the circle in 6 seconds at constant speed.
(a) Write a parameterization for the particle's motion.

static.solution:
(a) For any positive constant k, the parameterization x=-9\sin(kt)\quad y=9\cos(kt) moves counterclockwise on a circle of radius 9 starting at the point (0,9). We choose k to make the period 6 seconds. If k\cdot 6=2\pi, then k=\pi/3 and the parameterization is x=-9\sin\left(\frac {\pi t}{3}\right)\qquad y=9\cos \left(\frac {\pi t}{3}\right).
(b) Since it takes 6 seconds for the particle to go around the circle \mbox{Speed}=\frac{\mbox{Circumference of circle}}{6} = \frac {2\pi(9)}{6} = \frac {3\pi}{1}\mbox{ cm/sec}.
